scenarios.entry: A user generates keys with predictable entropy (zeroed test vectors, reused seeds, low-entropy `--entropy-file`).
scenarios.impact: Full key compromise; funds and identity stolen.
scenarios.mitigations: `new`/`restore` require entropy bytes (`--entropy-file` is explicit and hex-decoded); W0 vector suite pins key derivation; documentation forbids test vectors in production.
scenarios.residual: A user can still paste weak entropy manually.
scenarios.title: Weak or reused entropy at keygen

scenarios.entry: An attacker obtains `wallet-v1` keystore files from a backup or disk and runs offline guessing (hashcat-style).
scenarios.impact: Account compromise if the password is weak.
scenarios.mitigations: Argon2id `m=65536,t=3,p=4` (`KdfParams`), password minimum length 8, `password < len 8` refused with `error: usage: password must be at least 8 characters` (W1); keystore tests pin the KDF parameters.
scenarios.residual: Weak-but-compliant passwords remain guessable at lower cost.
scenarios.title: Offline brute force of a stolen keystore

scenarios.entry: A fake "wallet" tool or site asks for the keystore password or seed phrase (W1 review abuse case "phishing password").
scenarios.impact: Credential theft, full account compromise.
scenarios.mitigations: The wallet never prints seeds (`list` prints `entry=N`, `address=`, `public_key=` only — W0 log-scan NC); password is only read via `--password-file`, never argv; documentation warns users.
scenarios.residual: Users can still be tricked into typing a password into hostile software.
scenarios.title: Phishing password through a fake workflow

scenarios.entry: While the user moves the encoded payload across the air gap, the attacker swaps it for a payload paying a different destination (W1 review case "malicious payload swap").
scenarios.impact: The user signs a transaction they never intended.
scenarios.mitigations: W3 shows `chain/kind/fee/note` before signing and binds the signature to the decoded bytes (`payload_hash`); W1-FORMAT-v1 summary UX shows `kind`, `signer`, `chain`, `amount`, `destination`, `fee`, `nonce`, `memo`; envelope trailer checksum detects accidental truncation.
scenarios.residual: A user who approves without reading the summary is still exposed — mitigated operationally by the H0 review gate training.
scenarios.title: Malicious payload swapped in transit (QR / file)

scenarios.entry: An envelope produced for `auralite-test-1` is replayed against a different network's RPC.
scenarios.impact: Replay of a signed intent on another chain.
scenarios.mitigations: `submit` rechecks the chain id and refuses cross-chain submit (`error: refused: cross-chain submit: tx=…, wallet=…`, W2); signatures bind the chain id through `domain_message` (W1).
scenarios.residual: None known for cross-chain replay within AuraLite.
scenarios.title: Submitting an offline signature to the wrong network

scenarios.entry: An attacker takes bytes signed for one kind (e.g. `vote`) and presents them as another kind (`tx`) to a verifier that forgets the domain.
scenarios.impact: Forgery of a class of messages from one valid signature.
scenarios.mitigations: All signatures cover `chain || kind || message` (`domain_message`); W3 named control `verify_foreign_domain` proves a foreign domain fails `error: signature verification failed`; the frozen W1-FORMAT-v1 separates kinds and addresses.
scenarios.residual: New code paths that add signatures must call `verify_raw` with the same domain construction (enforced by reviews).
scenarios.title: Signature domain confusion (kind reuse)

scenarios.entry: A malicious node returns inflated `max_fee` estimates or wrong nonce to make the user overpay or stall.
scenarios.impact: Fee theft, stuck transactions.
scenarios.mitigations: W2 `encode`/`sign` enforce `--tip must not exceed --max-fee`; fee display is part of the summary the user approves; node software (D-phases) logs fee fields.
scenarios.residual: A user who blindly accepts suggested fees is still exposed.
scenarios.title: RPC node lies about fees or nonce

scenarios.entry: Flooding the node RPC (D5 limit: 100 req/s per IP) to exhaust CPU, disk or the mempool.
scenarios.impact: Node unavailability; mempool grows to 10,000 tx.
scenarios.mitigations: D5 rate limiting with the bounded mempool; p2p frame limits (N1 `MAX_FRAME`, handshakes); operational runbooks (H9 later).
scenarios.residual: Distributed floods can still degrade a single node.
scenarios.title: Denial of service against the RPC endpoint

scenarios.entry: A peer sends oversized or malformed frames, or surrounds the node to eclipse its view (W2 review case "hostile rpc peer frame").
scenarios.impact: Node crash, stale view, delayed consensus.
scenarios.mitigations: N1 bounded frames and handshake checks; N6/N7 verification chains; node restart drills (N8) cover recovery; W2 vectors pin frame rejection paths.
scenarios.residual: Small networks remain eclipse-prone by topology.
scenarios.title: Hostile p2p frames / eclipse attempt

scenarios.entry: A validator (or its stolen key) signs two conflicting blocks at the same height.
scenarios.impact: Consensus safety violation; chain halt or fork.
scenarios.mitigations: B-series consensus rules (commit-verify, unlock semantics); `aura-signer` hardware workflow with slot height binding (B11 artifact spec); slashing/double-sign logging planned (H6).
scenarios.residual: Key theft before detection (T9 test-keys case).
scenarios.title: Validator double-signing

scenarios.entry: A block proposer omits or reorders transactions (W2 review case "validator censorship").
scenarios.impact: Selective denial, MEV-style extraction.
scenarios.mitigations: Rotating proposers (B-series round-robin determinism), proposal hash visibility (`BlockCommitVerified`), mempool ordering rules; economic analysis planned (H6).
scenarios.residual: Bounded reordering inside a proposal window.
scenarios.title: Validator censorship / reordering

scenarios.entry: An attacker with old validator keys rewrites history from a snapshot (W2 review case "long-range snapshot").
scenarios.impact: Users following an old checkpoint accept a forged chain.
scenarios.mitigations: Explicit handoff receipts with `next_validator_root` (W2 vectors `receipt_round_7_*`); snapshot hashing in the DB; external review gate before trusting weak subjectivity parameters (H8).
scenarios.residual: Weak subjectivity remains a social assumption for light clients.
scenarios.title: Long-range or checkpoint rewrite

scenarios.entry: An operator account or CI job reads node key files from disk/backups.
scenarios.impact: Node impersonation, validator key misuse if co-hosted.
scenarios.mitigations: `init` refuses unsafe configurations (`error: refused: unsafe configuration`); key files documented as 0600; H7 will add HSM guidance and CI isolation.
scenarios.residual: Host root is always game over.
scenarios.title: Node key theft from the host

scenarios.entry: A maintainer swaps genesis bytes or a ceremony parameter between the reviewed text and the executed artifact (W2 review case "genesis ceremony forgery").
scenarios.impact: Network starts with hostile rules or balances.
scenarios.mitigations: D-phases pin the genesis document and validator root; the ceremony checklist (D-phase docs) demands N-of-M independent sha256 confirmations; `domain_message` genesis kind separates genesis signatures.
scenarios.residual: Colluding ceremony participants (threshold assumption).
scenarios.title: Genesis ceremony forgery

scenarios.entry: A crates.io/npm/PyPI dependency or a toolchain update ships malicious code that alters builds or fixtures.
scenarios.impact: Backdoored binaries; fabricated evidence.
scenarios.mitigations: Rust builds use a pinned toolchain (1.99.1); `Cargo.lock` is committed; generated fixtures are re-derivable from committed oracles (`tools/gen_*_vectors.py`) and pinned in `SHA256SUMS`; H1 will add `cargo-deny`/`cargo-audit`/SBOM/gitleaks.
scenarios.residual: Undetected upstream compromise before H1 automation.
scenarios.title: Dependency or toolchain compromise

scenarios.entry: An attacker submits a patch that subtly weakens a check (e.g. edits an oracle) while keeping tests green (W2 review case "compromised patch in review").
scenarios.impact: Silent regression of security properties.
scenarios.mitigations: Named mutation controls (`tools/nc_*.py`) pin that each gate is load-bearing; negative-control counts are audited (`tools/audit_closeout.py --strict`); phase patches carry receipts; source drift is recorded explicitly (`docs/evidence/review-w1-source-drift.txt`).
scenarios.residual: Reviewer bandwidth; social engineering of reviewers.
scenarios.title: Compromised patch or fixture in review

scenarios.entry: Someone edits `docs/evidence/**` or replaces a backup tarball to hide a failure.
scenarios.impact: False confidence in a broken build.
scenarios.mitigations: Every evidence bundle has `SHA256SUMS` over sources and logs; audit_closeout verifies receipt/patch/NC-log/evidence coherence per phase; W-tarballs are sha256-pinned in `*-tarball-sha256.txt` (verified in each restore drill).
scenarios.residual: An insider with full workspace access can rewrite history.
scenarios.title: Evidence tampering or rollback

scenarios.entry: Two honest builders get different binaries; a hostile build slips in unnoticed because nothing pins the output.
scenarios.impact: Users run a binary nobody audited.
scenarios.mitigations: Deterministic derivations are pinned as vectors (W-series); H7 will add two-host reproducible builds with matching sha256; toolchains pinned.
scenarios.residual: Rust/Cargo reproducibility is not yet enforced in CI (H7).
scenarios.title: Build non-reproducibility hides a swap

scenarios.entry: A password is passed as a CLI argument (visible in `ps`, shell history) or accidentally logged.
scenarios.impact: Credential leak on a shared host.
scenarios.mitigations: The CLI takes `--password-file` only (never a password argument); W0 log-scan control (`MnemonicInLog`) proves secrets are not in outputs; make logs pass the same scan.
scenarios.residual: A hostile local process can read the password file.
scenarios.title: Keystore password in argv or logs

scenarios.entry: A user imports an attacker-supplied keystore (e.g. a "recovery" service) that contains attacker-known keys or a hostile KDF downgrade.
scenarios.impact: The user stores funds on attacker-controlled keys.
scenarios.mitigations: `import`/`restore` recompute keys from the secret and print the derived `address=` for user comparison; keystore KDF parameters are validated on read (W1 refactor pinned them); `wallet-v1` JSON format is fixed.
scenarios.residual: Users may not compare addresses.
scenarios.title: Malicious keystore file from a third party

scenarios.entry: The user forgets the password or corrupts the keystore (W2 review case "lost password bricks account").
scenarios.impact: Permanent loss of access to funds.
scenarios.mitigations: Standard exit 69 `error: keystore: …` taxonomy keeps failures explicit; documentation demands backups of keystore + password hints; H9 incident playbook will cover recovery paths.
scenarios.residual: No recovery without the password (by design).
scenarios.title: Lost or wrong password bricks the account

scenarios.entry: A user typos a destination or misunderstands units (W2 review case "misuse sends funds wrong address").
scenarios.impact: Irreversible transfer to the wrong account.
scenarios.mitigations: The W1 summary UX shows `amount` and `destination` before signing; address checksums (`wallet-address-v1`) reject mistyped strings; `show` verifies decoded payloads before human approval.
scenarios.residual: Users can confirm the wrong address (H1-human factor training).
scenarios.title: CLI misuse sends funds to a wrong address

scenarios.entry: An insider constructs a bundle that claims threshold approvals without real member signatures (W4 review case "skip multi-approval").
scenarios.impact: Theft of shared funds with a fake quorum.
scenarios.mitigations: `msig-collect` verifies every approval signature and membership and enforces `threshold` (D-W4-1..4); the named W4 control proves `error: multisig: threshold not met (2/3)` is load-bearing; approvals bind the exact proposal and contract ids.
scenarios.residual: A quorum of real members can always act (governance assumption).
scenarios.title: Multi-approval bypass in the multisig contract

scenarios.entry: A removed member keeps signing proposals that old tooling still accepts (W4 review case "membership stays stale").
scenarios.impact: Ex-member moves funds after removal.
scenarios.mitigations: Rotation is a `rotate` proposal validated against the new descriptor (D-W4-3); the contract id changes with membership, and every approval binds the contract id (`error: multisig: proposal for a different contract`).
scenarios.residual: Off-chain tooling caching old contract ids must re-resolve.
scenarios.title: Membership stays stale after rotation

scenarios.entry: An attacker replays approvals for a proposal after its expiry or on another collection run (W4 review case "proposal replay after expiry").
scenarios.impact: Execution of stale intents.
scenarios.mitigations: Proposals carry `expiry` and `--height` checks refuse stale proposals (`error: multisig: proposal expired`); approvals bind the proposal id and contract id; a second collect of the same bundle is a duplicate (`error: multisig: duplicate approval`).
scenarios.residual: Replay protection across external execution layers belongs to the future on-chain multisig (H6/H8 review).
scenarios.title: Proposal replay after expiry

scenarios.entry: Fatigue or urgency makes a user confirm a summary that does not match their intent (W1 review case "human confirms what they did not read").
scenarios.impact: Signed hostile intent.
scenarios.mitigations: Fixed summary fields (kind, signer, chain, amount, destination, fee, nonce, memo) require explicit `--i-understand-testnet-only` on testnet commands; human-denied flow is a first-class path (`refused: human denied`).
scenarios.residual: Confirmation bias cannot be engineered away; W5 hardware confirmation (Stage 2) targets exactly this scenario.
scenarios.title: Human approves what they did not read

scenarios.entry: A hostile tool rewrites a keystore with weaker Argon2id parameters so that later cracking becomes cheap.
scenarios.impact: Cheap offline brute force after theft.
scenarios.mitigations: W1 refactor output pinned `KdfParams { m: 65536, t: 3, p: 4, salt: 32 bytes }`; keystore reads validate KDF fields; W1 fuzz vectors stress decode paths.
scenarios.residual: Out-of-repo tools can still write weak files.
scenarios.title: KDF parameters downgraded on import

scenarios.entry: Chunked QR codes (`ALO1:ii/nn:chunk`) are re-ordered, truncated or mixed between two sessions (W1 review case "payload corrupt QR framing").
scenarios.impact: Garbage or hostile bytes are decoded and possibly signed.
scenarios.mitigations: Decoder verifies index/count framing, single-session reassembly and the envelope trailer checksum; `parse` refuses bad framing with exit 69 `error: bad framing`; W3 vectors pin corrupted-encoding refusals.
scenarios.residual: A hostile re-framing that preserves checksums requires finding a BLAKE3 collision (assumed infeasible).
scenarios.title: QR payload framing corruption

scenarios.entry: An operator fabricates a snapshot chain (W2 review case "snapshot chain evidence fake") to make a broken state look checkpointed.
scenarios.impact: False recovery point; rollbacks to hostile state.
scenarios.mitigations: Snapshot hash chain is pinned in W2 vectors (`snapshot_chain_broken_link` refuses broken links); receipts carry `snapshot_root`; evidence bundles pin generator hashes.
scenarios.residual: A collusion of snapshot producers can fake their own chain.
scenarios.title: Snapshot chain evidence fake

scenarios.entry: `insecure-test-kdf`, testing entropy or fixtures accidentally ship in a release profile (W1 review case "test scaffolding leaks").
scenarios.impact: Known-weak keys or parameters in production wallets.
scenarios.mitigations: `KdfParams::testing` is gated behind `cfg(feature = "insecure-test-kdf")`; tests are `#![cfg(feature = "insecure-test-kdf")]`; release checklist (WIP_SECURITY_AND_W1.md) forbids the feature outside tests.
scenarios.residual: Manual release discipline until H1 CI automation.
scenarios.title: Test scaffolding leaks into production

scenarios.entry: Logs or metrics include keys, passwords or user identifiers (W1 review case "PII in observability output").
scenarios.impact: Mass credential or privacy leak via log aggregation.
scenarios.mitigations: CLI prints only whitelisted fields (entry/address/public_key); W0 log-scan NC (`MnemonicInLog`) enforces "no mnemonic in logs"; audit evidence contains only public test material.
scenarios.residual: Operators may add verbose logging in the future — the H7 access log requirement covers detection.
scenarios.title: PII or secrets in observability output

scenarios.entry: An operator runs a node with debug endpoints open or a devnet key in a public network (W2 review case "unsafe configuration in production").
scenarios.impact: Remote compromise of node keys and state.
scenarios.mitigations: `init` refuses unsafe configurations (`error: refused: unsafe configuration`); `preflight` verifies config keys; runbooks call out the devnet-only markers.
scenarios.residual: Post-start configuration edits are out of scope of `init`.
scenarios.title: Unsafe node configuration in production
